- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward adjustment of 2–5% for next forecast.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp drop or mean reversion, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- After a strong upward spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak unless sentiment remains bullish.
- When sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for potential drop.
- If true outcome deviates from model by >5% in first 3–5 days, assume model is lagging; adjust forecast to align with recent 3–5 day true trend.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 1.00 (strong bullish) followed by sharp drop, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 3–5% after 2–3 bullish days.
- For 30-day horizon, if model is flat or slowly rising while true outcome shows volatility, assume model is ignoring sentiment; adjust to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.
